title: Ordering a Cake at Fenner's Bakery
context: A customer at a bakery counter places an order for a large cake and settles the details with the baker.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Good morning, Fenner's Bakery. How can I help?

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Hello. I'd like to order a cake for a party, if that's possible.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Of course. Let me just find the order book — here we are. Can I take a name first?

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Yes, it's Beckett. Marilyn Beckett. That's B, E, C, K, E, T, T.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Beckett. Thank you. And what's the cake for? A birthday?

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Well, everyone keeps calling it a birthday party, but it isn't — it's my mother's retirement. She's finishing at the hospital after thirty-one years.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: A retirement, then. I'll write that down. And how many people are we feeding?

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: There'll be about thirty at the party, but a lot of them are children, so I think a cake for twenty-five would be plenty.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Twenty-five it is. Now, our sponge cakes come in three flavours — chocolate, lemon, or carrot.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Chocolate, I think. Actually, no. My mother doesn't really like chocolate. Could we do the lemon one?

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Lemon, lovely.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Hmm — although, sorry, could I change that once more? Carrot. She's talked about your carrot cake for years.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Carrot. I'll write it in capital letters so nobody gets confused. And would you like anything written on top?

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Yes please. Just 'Well done, Sylvia'.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Well done, Sylvia. Now, is there anything I need to know about allergies?

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Yes — one of my aunts can't have nuts at all. Not even a trace of them.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: That's fine. We make a nut-free version first thing in the morning, before anything with nuts in it comes out of the store cupboard. There's no extra charge for that.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: That's a relief. I was expecting it to cost more.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Not at all. Right, the price. A carrot cake for twenty-five is normally fifty-five pounds, and the icing with writing on it adds another five. So sixty pounds altogether.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Sixty. That's fine.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: And we ask for a deposit of ten pounds today, with the rest when you collect it.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Can I pay the deposit by card?

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Card is fine. Now — when do you need it?

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: The party's on the Saturday. Could I pick it up on the Saturday morning? That would be easiest for me.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: We're only open until twelve on Saturdays, and Saturday mornings here are chaos, to be honest with you. I'd much rather you took it on the Friday and kept it somewhere cool overnight. It'll be just as good.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Friday, then. That works too.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Friday, and I'll have it ready from ten. One more thing — it comes in a big box, so bring the car if you can. It won't sit on a bicycle.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: I'll drive over, don't worry.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: Perfect. Oh, and can I ask how you heard about us? We're trying to work out where our customers come from.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: My sister lives on the next street and she's been coming here for years. She's the one who told me about the carrot cake.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: A recommendation, then. That's what we like to hear. I'll give you a slip with the order number on it — it's 4218 — and just bring that with you on the day.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: 4218. Thank you very much.

script.speaker: Baker
script.text: See you on Friday, then. Have a lovely party.

questions.instruction: Complete the order form below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.explanation: The customer gives her name and then spells it: "it's Beckett. Marilyn Beckett. That's B, E, C, K, E, T, T."

questions.sentence: Occasion the cake is for: a ___
questions.explanation: The baker guesses a birthday, but the customer corrects him: "it isn't — it's my mother's retirement." The second word is the answer.
Thirty people are coming, but many are children, so the customer says "a cake for twenty-five would be plenty," and the baker writes that down.
The customer changes her mind twice — chocolate, then lemon — before settling on "Carrot. She's talked about your carrot cake for years."
The cake is fifty-five pounds and the writing adds five, so the baker gives the total: "So sixty pounds altogether."
The baker asks for "a deposit of ten pounds today, with the rest when you collect it," so only part of the price is paid now.

questions.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.question: When does the baker advise the customer to collect the cake?
questions.explanation: The customer asks for Saturday morning, but the baker replies, "I'd much rather you took it on the Friday," and she agrees.

questions.question: What does the customer tell the baker about nuts?
options: one of the guests cannot eat them
she would like some on the cake
questions.explanation: She says "one of my aunts can't have nuts at all," and the baker adds that a nut-free cake carries "no extra charge," so the third option is wrong.

questions.question: Why does the baker suggest the customer brings a car?
options: the box is too large for a bicycle
the bakery is far from the bus stop
the cake must be kept in a fridge
questions.explanation: The baker explains, "it comes in a big box, so bring the car if you can. It won't sit on a bicycle."

questions.question: How did the customer hear about the bakery?
questions.explanation: She says her sister "has been coming here for years. She's the one who told me about the carrot cake," which the baker calls a recommendation.
